imagine_stars.txt l.50 'As the protostar gains mass, its core gets hotter and more dense ... 15 million Kelvin in the core for fusion to begin' plus nasa_stars.txt on hydrogen nuclei squeezed into helium releasing energy support s10/s11 word for word ('degrees' vs kelvin is immaterial at this scale).

imagine_stars.txt equilibrium quote and nasa_stars.txt 'Nuclear fusion releases energy, which heats the star and prevents it from further collapsing' support s03/s12/s37. 'Lasts millions of years' understates the Sun's ~10 billion but is not false; 'millions or even billions of years' would be more informative. 'Darkest object' / 'soft cloud of dust' are rhetorical, not factual claims.
nasa_stars.txt 'This is the longest phase of a star's life' and 'Our Sun is roughly midway through its main sequence stage' plus imagine_stars.txt support s13 exactly.

Round 2: s14 now says 'depends, above all, on mass', which matches the newly added quote imagine_stars.txt l.45 'The fate and life of a star depends primarily on it's mass' and nasa_stars.txt l.383 (mass 'determines how rapidly it runs through its supply'). The burn-rate and lifetime figures in s14/s15 are quoted directly (nasa_stars.txt l.383, imagine_stars.txt l.51).

nasa_stars.txt 'white dwarf, a roughly Earth-sized stellar cinder that gradually cools' and '(This will be the fate of our Sun...)' support s16; 'finish quietly' is fair relative to a supernova (imagine_stars.txt: the star sheds its mass as a planetary nebula).

Round 2: s17 now says 'Stars born with more than about eight times the Sun's mass end their lives by exploding', which is what imagine_sn.txt ('8 times or more massive ... go supernova') and nasa_bh_types.txt l.379 ('more than eight times the Sun's mass ... explodes as a supernova') say. It no longer excludes white-dwarf (Type Ia) explosions. 'Born with' (initial mass) is a fair reading of both sources.

Contested claim narrated with hedges ('probably', 'around twenty ... or more', 'Exactly where that line sits is still being studied'; s02 'could end'). nasa_bh_types.txt l.379 and imagine_stars.txt l.63 give ~20 solar masses; imagine_sn.txt gives 15+, so the source disagreement itself justifies the hedge. Wording stays within the evidence.

nasa_stars.txt (core runs out of hydrogen) and imagine_stars.txt l.53/60 (inner layers collapse, core squished, pressure and temperature rise, outer layers expand; high-mass stars become red supergiants) support every clause of s18.

imagine_stars.txt (helium to carbon, carbon to neon) and nasa_stars.txt l.390 (carbon to oxygen, neon, magnesium 'which will become future fuel'; chain continues until silicon fuses into iron; 'each new fuel buys it less and less time'; 'runs out of fuel in a matter of days') support s19/s20.

imagine_stars.txt 'fusing iron requires an input of energy, rather than producing excess energy. With a core full of iron, the star will lose the fight against gravity' supports s21 directly; Chandra and NASA quotes agree.
imagine_sn.txt: 'In less than a second, the star begins the final phase of gravitational collapse. The core temperature rises to over 100 billion degrees' matches s22.

nasa_stars.txt: iron core collapses, 'then it rebounds. This change creates a shock wave that travels outward through the star. The result is a huge explosion called a supernova' and 'The core survives as an incredibly dense remnant, either a neutron star or a black hole' support s23, s29 and the hedged summary in s38 ('can fall into a black hole').

esahubble_sn.txt: 'often briefly outshines an entire galaxy, before fading from view over several weeks or months'; s24 says 'can outshine ... before fading over weeks or months', which is within the evidence.

nasa_crab.txt: 1054, Chinese astronomers, 'guest star' visible in the daytime for nearly a month, gave rise to the Crab Nebula, 'a six-light-year-wide remnant'. s25/s26 match; 'expanding' is not in the quote (only the pulsar wisps are called expanding, l.406) but is standard and harmless.

chandra_casa_life.txt l.93: the Chandra image shows 'silicon (red), sulfur (yellow), calcium (green) and iron (purple)' in the remains of the explosion; s27 matches. r_casa is that 2017 Chandra element map. Its blue is the blast wave, not an element, so the on-screen colour key must not imply otherwise.
